answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create urgency, but the 94% capacity utilization makes delivery risk acute. Switching to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2) is too dangerous—they missed SLA in 3 of 4 quarters on a non-critical line; on a critical component at full load, failure cascades. Renewing incumbent (memory_c1) preserves stability but leaves cost pressure unaddressed. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing without narrowing scope, and memory_c4 demonstrates the incumbent will move on price and terms under benchmark pressure. Negotiation leverages the market intelligence (memory_c4 success) to extract the cost reduction we need while keeping the supply stable and integrated. Verification of memory_c2 and memory_c4 confirms both the risk ceiling and the incumbent's demonstrated flexibility. Adding a second source (memory_c3) is a sound long-term strategy but consumes the one decision slot and doesn't address the immediate 18% target. Deferring is not viable—the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. Aggressive negotiation against benchmarks is the highest-probability path to hit cost targets while preserving the delivery buffer we cannot afford to lose.
